posts.author: Ash24
posts.body:
Hi all,
I am looking to make a 2D turn-based RPG and as a newbie (kind of) to RPG Maker and game dev in general I could do with a bit of advice.
Bit of a background about me; I have a little experience with RPG Maker (namely a number of half finished projects in RPG Maker 95 many moons ago, and messing about with 2003 a bit) and I am not exactly a great programmer either (did a few courses in Java and Python a few years ago but that's about as far as my knowledge goes).
I want to make a game where certain weapons, items and skills can be used in the field to solve puzzles and such, basically combining a turn-based RPG with some light Zelda elements (a bit like Final Fantasy Mystic Quest I suppose). Stuff like using a fire spell to melt ice, using bombs to blow up holes in a cracked wall, a whip or grappling hook to cross pits, etc.
Is this something that can be done in RPG Maker? If so, which version would be best to use to achieve this? (I own 2003 and XP on Steam but I am going to assume that these are not going to cut it).
Any help or advice would be much appreciated!
Thanks!
Ash

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
To be pedantic for a bit, so long as you chose to go with either MV or MZ, the code is entirely open for you to edit. So the question of "can it be done" is always "yes." but of course the more appropriate question is "Is it practical to do it in the engine?"
In this case:
Ash24 said:
weapons, items and skills can be used in the field
Click to expand...
Yes.
You would need to be able to set up the events yourself, and likely a few plugins to assist with puzzle solving would make it much easier, but in general, most of what you described is not too difficult.
However, if you are new to RPG Maker (for the most part), it is not recommended you start with that. Eventing those types of things will require some more advanced understanding of the engine, including plugins and maybe utilizing script calls a little to make things more efficient. It would be far better to start with something that just utilizes the base event commands of the engine so that you can familiarize yourself with the tool that you are using. Learn the fundamentals first so you can build on your knowledge, rather than start with something complicated and burn the house down.
Ash24 said:
which version would be best to use to achieve this?
Click to expand...
MV or MZ.
We just had a thread about which is better (MV or MZ), and we've had a hundred more in the past, so if you can't decide which of those to buy, just google it and you'll get a long list of reasons as to why one is better than the other.
MZ is newer, MV has better/easier support.

posts.author: Traverse
posts.body:
Ash24 said:
Is this something that can be done in RPG Maker? If so, which version would be best to use to achieve this? (I own 2003 and XP on Steam but I am going to assume that these are not going to cut it).
Click to expand...
Yes, though you might find it easier in some engine versions than in others.
The engines from XP onwards are all pretty customizable to the point you can do almost anything, because XP was when they opened up the code of the engine via the script editor. The scripts you see in the XP script editor (and VX and VX Ace script editors) are most of the base engine - the rest of the code is in the RGSS DLL files, which are not open for editing (but also probably not what you'd be interested in if you're just looking to implement the gameplay features you mentioned).
MV and MZ don't have a script editor but that's also because the engine code for those is 100% open and available in the .js JavaScript files you see in a game's project folder (the ones like rpg_scenes.js and rpg_window.js). You can open them up in a text editor or IDE of your choice to mess around with them. Instead of a script editor, MV/MZ has a "plugins" feature where you can put extra .js JavaScript files into the "plugins" folder and enable them from the engine's plugins manager to extend the functionality of the engine.
......Whether you will actually need to mess around with the code of the base engine will depend on what exact features what you're envisioning.
If you're thinking of having Zelda-type pixel free movement (i.e. not constrained to tiles) you WILL need to mess around with the base engine, as it's otherwise locked to tile-based movement. There are already a bunch of those kinds of plugins/script floating around, pixel-movement is a popular feature, people have made scripts for it for every version of the engine.
On the other hand, if it's just interacting with elements on the map at pre-determined places, you can probably do that without any messing around with the base engine. The inbuilt mapping/eventing system is likely be enough for it.
Apart from pixel movement, a general rule of thumb is that anything that involves the menus/text boxes, the title screen or the battle system typically needs messing with the engine.
